clue.text: Where one may see drinks dispensers in prison?

definitions.text: Where one may see drinks dispensers
definitions.meaning: bartenders dispensing drinks stand behind the bars of a pub
the idiom for being locked up in jail

explanation.surface: A wry question about bar staff who have ended up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'bars' as pub counters; the second as the iron bars of a cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind bars is the everyday idiom for being imprisoned, and also literally where bartenders work.

clue.text: Needle person supported by family

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top, held up by the second

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Someone who needles, backed up by relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' looks like a verb, to annoy; it is the noun, a blunt sewing needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a thick blunt needle for threading tape or cord through fabric.

clue.text: Farm animal, slaughtered if here

indicators.note: butchered, so the letters are cut up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A grim warning that a farm animal will be killed if it stays.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow that has not yet calved, kept as livestock.

clue.text: Uncooperative union may cause a financial problem

parts.note: a negative attitude is an unhelpful, uncooperative one
Equity is the British actors' trade union

explanation.surface: An awkward trade union could trigger money troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the trade union for British actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Negative equity is owing more on a mortgage than the property is worth, a money trouble for homeowners.

clue.text: Old curiosities in remarkably barbaric boxing clubs

indicators.note: the rearranged word surrounds the letter, as a box encloses its contents
done in a striking way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Antiques found among savage boxing clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' turns BARBARIC into BRIABRAC; 'boxing' puts C inside it. 'Boxing clubs' looks like gyms for fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bric-a-brac is miscellaneous ornaments and trinkets of small value, often old curios.

clue.text: Quick attack seizing power

indicators.note: the raid grabs the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A swift assault that takes control.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid is a synonym for fast or speedy.

clue.text: Tennis champion's good service

parts.note: the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Praise for a tennis star's fine serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a tennis serve but means an armed service, the RAF (Royal Air Force).
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf won twenty-two Grand Slam singles titles, a celebrated tennis champion.

clue.text: Croatian's battered mac

indicators.note: knocked about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Croatian's worn-out mackintosh.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is': Croatian is battered into a mac.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac, short for mackintosh, is a waterproof coat worn against rain.

clue.text: Swimmers must secure one object — that's very difficult

indicators.note: the swimmers have to hold the other pieces firmly within them

parts.note: fish are swimmers
I is the Roman numeral for one
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A rule that swimmers must fasten one item, a tough task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a physical thing, but here means a goal or purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiendish puzzle is devilishly hard or extremely complex.

clue.text: Cyborgs dope him in motion picture

indicators.note: moving, so the letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Robots drug a man in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in motion picture' looks like one phrase, a film, but 'in motion' is the anagram signal and 'picture' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodbye, Mr Chips is a 1939 film about a schoolmaster, a motion picture.

clue.text: Working on ruin close to Heidelberg

parts.note: to do in is slang for to wreck or ruin

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so this takes the end of Heidelberg

explanation.surface: Someone busy restoring a ruin near the German city of Heidelberg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like nearness in place but picks the last letter, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing describes being busy at a task, a synonym for working, as in 'what are you doing?'

clue.text: Is impressed by better jam

indicators.note: the first word is pressed into the middle of the synonym that follows

parts.note: to better something is to improve it

explanation.surface: Someone is struck by a superior jam, perhaps a preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' reads as a preserve, but it is the musicians' verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians who jam play spontaneously without a score, which is improvising.

clue.text: Disinclination to act in time to catch it on the way back

indicators.note: the time word holds the following piece inside it, as a hand catches a ball

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: travelling back means the word it is read right to left

explanation.surface: Reluctance to do anything, captured on a return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disinclination to act' is the physics idea used of people; 'it on the way back' must be read before 'to catch' applies.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia in people is sluggishness or a tendency to stay inactive, a reluctance to stir.

clue.text: Gathered action involves French duke

indicators.note: to involve here is to wrap around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
duc is the French word for duke

explanation.surface: Someone collected that a scheme concerns a French nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathered' looks like collected, but here means worked out or understood.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather a fact from evidence is to infer it, a synonym for deduced.

clue.text: As every other represented through time?

indicators.note: presented again in a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about recurring alternately across the passage of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the years means across a long span of time, gradually through time.

clue.text: Hotel diner with can staggering in bar

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: reeling unsteadily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hotel guest staggers into a bar with a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb-noun obstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is an obstacle or barrier, and a hindrance is something that obstructs.

clue.text: Culprit given fine having split old electric guitar

indicators.note: the letter comes between the two pieces, dividing them

parts.note: Fender is a well-known maker of electric guitars
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer fined for breaking a vintage guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having split' puts F between O and FENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who has committed a crime or wrong, the guilty party.

clue.text: Stray may produce a howl climbing about on a tavern's roof

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a yell is a loud cry or howl
ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: the roof of a word in a down answer is its top, first letter

explanation.surface: A wandering cat yowling on a pub roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns YELL into LLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley cat is a stray urban cat with no owner.

clue.text: Scale of money spent may represent this?

definitions.text: Scale of money spent may represent this?

indicators.note: spent money is used up and scattered, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a scale of spending reveals a bad bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SCALE OF MONEY is the answer, and an amount of money spent can itself be such a misguided saving.
explanation.definitionFit: A false economy is a saving that costs more in the long run, a judgment about how much is spent.

clue.text: Arrived with artist's photographic device

parts.note: came means arrived
RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone turned up with a painter's camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the apparatus used to take photographs.

clue.text: Entertained, in the morning, American editor

parts.note: a.m. marks morning hours

explanation.surface: An American editor was diverted early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused means diverted or kept pleasantly occupied.

clue.text: Top four leaving administration

indicators.note: the numeral departs from the longer word, so its letters are removed

parts.note: the executive is the administrative branch of a government or firm
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four senior figures quit the management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like senior, but is slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is British slang for to kill them, as an executioner does.

clue.text: Girl in lifestyle magazine, ultimate in fashion

parts.note: Elle is a well-known fashion and lifestyle magazine

indicators.note: the ultimate of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A young woman featured in a glossy magazine, the last word in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate in fashion' looks like the height of style but just picks N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a girl's first name; crosswords define names by the kind of person.

clue.text: Get back about allegation

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a claim is an assertion or allegation

explanation.surface: Recovering something in connection with an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim property is to recover or retrieve what was yours.

clue.text: French actor gripping whip hard in sporting contest

indicators.note: the actor holds the following pieces inside his name

parts.note: Alain Delon was a famous French film actor
a cat is short for cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A French actor clutching a whip during an athletics event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts CATH inside DELON.
explanation.definitionFit: The decathlon is a ten-event athletics competition, a contest of sport.

clue.text: Aims of some inside a seminary

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The goals held by certain people within a religious college.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas can mean intentions or plans, as in 'I had ideas of travelling', so aims.

clue.text: Reportedly lawful ceremony

indicators.note: as reported in speech, the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: something lawful is right or rightful

explanation.surface: A ceremony said to be legal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal ritual or solemn observance, such as a religious ceremony.

clue.text: See below platform

parts.note: under means below
a stand is a raised platform

explanation.surface: An instruction to look beneath a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like look, but means grasp, as in 'I see'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'I see' means one grasps the point, so see is a synonym for comprehend.
